extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, judges, and law students studying patent litigation procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing presentation of evidence, jury instructions, burden of proof, and allocation of court-vs-jury questions in U.S. patent infringement trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff's proof of damages and causation
rubrics_metrics.description: After he has shown that his entire loss has resulted from the infringement, and has refuted all the defendant's suggestions as to contributory causes, he is not obliged to controvert all other possible causes and exclude every hypothesis except that which he maintains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inquiry is to be conducted on the same principles as any other investigation into an amount of damages, and especially when the infringement has been wilful must the evidence be liberally interpreted in favor of the plaintiff. The plaintiff is not obliged to produce such testimony as removes all reasonable doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order in which evidence is produced
rubrics_metrics.description: When the pleadings are closed upon the general issue, the plaintiff goes forward at the trial, and must introduce the evidence required to make out a prima facie case upon all the averments in his declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letters-patent, or a certified copy thereof, being produced and offered, sufficiently prove their own validity as well as the patentability of the invention. The plaintiff must then prove his title, either by the patent if he is the patentee, or by the proper documentary evidence if he is an assignee or grantee. Evidence of the performance of the infringing acts by the defendant, and of the identity of the invention which he sells or uses with that covered by the plaintiff's patent, must be also laid before the jury, and the data given for an estimate of the damages sustained. The defendant must reply by counter-proof; if he files a special plea, the order of procedure is reversed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts having held that the patent is prima facie evidence on points of validity, novelty, utility, and sufficiency of specification, extraneous testimony of these matters is unnecessary though frequently practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some writers assert extraneous testimony on novelty/utility/completeness should be presented, but judicially the patent itself is prima facie evidence on these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal courts and nonsuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal courts have no authority to order a nonsuit of the plaintiff, though his evidence may be plainly insufficient to warrant a verdict in his favor, but must submit the issue to the jury on such proof as has been offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defendant may request the court to instruct the jury that the testimony will not support a verdict for the plaintiff; refusal to give such instruction when proper is error. If the jury disregard a correct instruction and render a verdict for plaintiff, the court cannot accept it but must set it aside and order a new trial. Where any evidence is introduced by the plaintiff which could reasonably tend to support his cause, it must be submitted to the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's charge to the jury must be limited and clear
rubrics_metrics.description: The charge of the judge to the jury must arise out of and be limited to the questions in controversy and the evidence produced, and must be sufficiently full and clear to serve them as an intelligible guide in arriving at their verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General abstract discussions are improper. Either party may request instructions; failure to comply is regarded as refusal and must be excepted to at trial or the objection is waived. When a request is granted, exact form need not be followed so long as the instruction given comports with justice and affords an opportunity to render a proper verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for instructions and timing of exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal to give desired instructions may be taken advantage of on writ of error, but the exception must be noted at the time so the error can be corrected while the jury are at bar, or the objection will be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with requests to charge is equivalent to a refusal; errors or refusals not excepted to at the time are waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court vs jury: general allocation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the enumerated defences certain questions arise whose decision is within the province of the court, while others are to be determined by the jury; the general distinction is that which separates matters of law from matters of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular allocation is stated in connection with each defence: the court defines legal concepts and instructs; the jury determines factual application under those instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive act: court defines, jury decides application
rubrics_metrics.description: On the defence denying that the invention originated in an inventive act, the court defines the nature of an inventive act and of its result; the jury decide whether the patented invention is due to such an act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the defence admits an inventive act but denies performance by the alleged inventor (derivation), the court describes attributes; the jury determine whether the alleged inventor performed the act or derived it from another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/anticipation and diligence (prior inventor issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defence avers a prior inventor reduced the same act to practice or was using reasonable diligence, the court declares at what stage conception becomes complete and what diligence is required; the jury find whether prior conception or reduction to practice occurred and whether diligence was sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury decides whether the supposed prior inventor anticipated the plaintiff's inventor and whether reduction to practice or diligent efforts preceded the plaintiff's production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable class and combination questions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defence denies the invention is embraced in the patentable classes, the court determines from the patent the character of the invention and from the law whether it is included; the jury render a verdict in pursuance of that finding unless terms of art require the jury to pass on meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention purports to be a combination, additional questions of fact (effect and operation of mechanical contrivances) arise and must be passed on by the jury under court instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (prior patent/publication/use)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the defence denying novelty the court defines the attributes of novelty and the essential qualities of a prior use or prior publication and decides whether the claims of a prior patent cover the same invention; the jury find whether the prior patent/publication/use existed so as to render the invention accessible to the public before conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity of prior and present inventions, and whether printed publications describe the same invention, are questions for the jury where differences exist on their face or in expert judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility as mixed question: court defines, jury finds
rubrics_metrics.description: On the defence denying utility the court declares in what utility consists and directs the jury to find accordingly if the invention is manifestly frivolous or injurious; otherwise the jury determine whether the invention is practically available for any useful purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility is ordinarily a jury question; in some circumstances questions of uselessness may be decided by the court as a matter of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment: court defines doctrine, jury decides intent and facts
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defence alleges the inventor abandoned the invention to the public, the court defines abandonment and the presumptions from public use or sale; the jury pass upon questions of intention and occurrence of public sale/use constituting abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motive for delay in applying for a patent while the invention is in use and continuity questions of applications are for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and ambiguity of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: On defences alleging fraud or ambiguity in the specification the court construes the language and defines attributes of a sufficient description; the jury decide whether the specification discloses the invention so persons skilled in the art can practice it and whether concealment or redundancy resulted from intention to deceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a specification enables one skilled in the art to practise the invention is a question of fact for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive or ambiguous claims and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are alleged excessive the court construes the claim and fixes the standard by which diligence in filing any necessary disclaimer is to be measured; the jury decide whether the claim exceeds the actual invention and whether delay in filing a disclaimer is unreasonable. For ambiguous claims, the court interprets the claim as far as capable of interpretation and the jury follow that interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What constitutes unreasonable delay in filing a disclaimer is a mixed question of law and fact for the jury under court instructions; under some circumstances it may be a question of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender/annulment/repeal of patent (effect on rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a defence resting upon surrender, annulment, or repeal the court declares the law governing surrender and its effect upon existing rights; the jury determine whether the patent has thus been cancelled or is extinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings may be largely pro forma where evidence is record-based, but courts instruct juries on the legal effect of such records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue patents and scope/fraud issues
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defence alleges wrongful re-issue the court decides legal requisites of a legal patent, whether claims of a re-issue depart from the original invention, and whether re-issue was broader or obtained with fraudulent intent; the jury find whether legal requisites existed and whether the re-issue is identical or broader and whether intent was fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a re-issue departs from the original, or was obtained fraudulently, are jury questions under the court's instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of plaintiff's and defendant's inventions (infringement identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The court defines the patented invention as indicated by the language of the claims; the jury judge whether the invention so defined covers the art or article employed by the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identity question, if the patent is in evidence and not excluded, may be submitted to the jury under court instruction; whether the defendant infringes is a jury question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal attributes of infringing acts and joint/employee liability
rubrics_metrics.description: The court declares the legal attributes of an infringing act, the circumstances under which an employee is or is not responsible for obedience to employer's commands, and what degree of complicity renders one liable for infringement when completed by acts of others; the jury decide whether the defendant's acts were true infringements according to these doctrines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions of inducement, contributory infringement, and agent/employee liability are for the jury to resolve under legal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term expiration and interaction with foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: On the defence that the patent term had expired the court informs the jury when the patent would expire of its own limitation, what effect a prior foreign patent to the same inventor having a shorter term would produce, and whether the foreign patent covers the same invention; the jury find whether a prior foreign patent existed and whether the infringing act anticipated expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juries determine fact of foreign patent grant and its timing/effect under court instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization/license defense (ownership and scope of license)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the defence is that the defendant's use was authorized by the owner, the court declares the legal rights of part owners or licensees, interprets instruments or contracts, and defines acts empowered; the jury pass upon existence/authenticity of conveyances, identity of parties, and correspondence of defendant's acts with those permitted by his grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of instruments is for the court; existence and application of permissions are factual matters for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations defence
rubrics_metrics.description: On the defence resting upon the Statute of Limitations the court construes the statute; the jury decide whether the suit was instituted within the time prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of the statute is legal; timeliness and facts are for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel defence
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defence avers the plaintiff is estopped the court explains the doctrine of estoppel, interprets written instruments out of which an estoppel is said to have arisen, and defines any legal duty of the plaintiff by the neglect of which the defendant claims he was misled; the jury determine whether the estoppel exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court provides legal framework; jury decides factual existence and effect of alleged estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed verdict/demurrer to evidence in law actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a demurrer to evidence in an action at law the judge must decide whether the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case, and if not must charge the jury to find for the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is offered and excluded, plaintiff's case fails and no nonsuit is permitted but the court directs a verdict for defendant. Where evidence is submitted to the jury without objection, identity and related questions are for their decision under court instruction.
